title: Prisma Client Queries
description: Learn to read data with findMany, findUnique, findFirst, and understand when to use each query method.

data.text: Prisma Client provides three primary methods for reading data: `findMany`, `findUnique`, and `findFirst`. Each method has a specific use case depending on whether you are querying by a unique field or applying filters.
`findMany` returns an array of records. It is the most common query method and supports filtering, sorting, and pagination.

data.title: findMany Example

items: **findUnique** — Requires a unique field in the `where` clause. Throws if no record is found.
**findFirst** — Returns the first record matching the `where` clause, or `null` if none found.

data.title: findUnique Example
data.content: Fetch a user by unique email.

data.title: Note
data.text: `findUnique` requires a field marked with `@unique` in your schema. If you need to query by a non-unique field, use `findFirst`.
